content: Nicotine oral inhalation is prescribed to assist individuals in quitting smoking. It is intended to be used in conjunction with a comprehensive smoking cessation program, which may include support groups, counseling, or specific behavioral modification techniques. This medication belongs to a class of drugs known as smoking cessation aids. It functions by delivering nicotine to the body, which helps alleviate withdrawal symptoms associated with smoking cessation and reduces the urge to smoke. Nicotine oral inhalation is available as a cartridge that is inhaled through the mouth using a specialized inhaler. It is essential to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the medication exactly as directed, without exceeding or reducing the prescribed dose or frequency. Your doctor will provide guidance on the number of nicotine cartridges to use daily and may adjust your dose based on your smoking urges. After 12 weeks of use, once your body has adapted to not smoking, your doctor may gradually reduce your dose over the next 6 to 12 weeks until you no longer require nicotine inhalation. Follow your doctor’s instructions for tapering your nicotine dose. The nicotine in the cartridges is released through frequent puffing over approximately 20 minutes. You can use a cartridge all at once or in shorter sessions until the nicotine is depleted. Experiment with different schedules to determine what works best for you. Request a copy of the manufacturer’s patient information from your pharmacist or doctor, and carefully read the instructions for using the inhaler. Ask your healthcare provider to demonstrate the correct technique and practice using the inhaler under their supervision. If you have not successfully quit smoking after 4 weeks, consult your doctor. They can help identify potential barriers to quitting and develop a new plan to try again. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before using nicotine oral inhalation, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to nicotine, menthol, or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking or plan to take. Be sure to mention antidepressants such as amitriptyline, amoxapine, clomipramine, desipramine, doxepin, imipramine, nortriptyline, protriptyline, and trimipramine, as well as theophylline. Your doctor may need to adjust the dosages of your medications after you stop smoking. Inform your doctor if you have recently experienced a heart attack or if you have a history of asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), heart disease, angina, irregular heartbeat, circulation problems (e.g., Buerger’s disease or Raynaud’s phenomenon), hyperthyroidism, pheochromocytoma, insulin-dependent diabetes, ulcers, high blood pressure, or kidney or liver disease. Additionally, notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using nicotine inhalation, contact your doctor immediately, as nicotine may harm the fetus. It is crucial to stop smoking entirely while using nicotine inhalation. Continuing to smoke while using this medication may result in side effects. Be aware that you may still experience some withdrawal symptoms, such as dizziness, anxiety, sleep disturbances, depression, fatigue, and muscle pain, even while using nicotine inhalation. If these symptoms occur, consult your doctor about adjusting your nicotine dose. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, you may continue your normal diet while using this medication. Nicotine oral inhalation may cause minor side effects. Notify your doctor if any of the following symptoms are severe or persistent: irritation in the mouth and throat, cough, runny nose, changes in taste, jaw, neck, or back pain, dental issues, sinus pressure and pain, headache, tingling or burning sensations in the hands or feet, or gas. Some side effects can be serious. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience a rapid heart rate. If you notice any unusual problems while using this medication, inform your doctor. Store all components of the nicotine inhaler, including used and unused cartridges, out of reach of children and pets. Keep the mouthpiece in its plastic storage case and store the cartridges at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (avoid storing them in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on safe disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Symptoms of overdose may include paleness, cold sweat, nausea, drooling, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhea, headache, dizziness, hearing and vision problems, uncontrollable shaking, confusion, weakness, or seizures. Keep all appointments with your doctor while using this medication. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
